bullet_points: Download 200 evenly spaced VTK snapshots (indices 18903 to 19898, step 5) from the HuggingFace dataset to the user-provided data directory `/home/node/work/projects/ns_lagrangian_v1/data/`. Skip downloading if the file already exists.
Implement a robust download mechanism (e.g., using `urllib` or `requests` with retries) to handle the ~8GB total download.
Implement utility functions to read a VTK file, compute the velocity gradient, vorticity, Q-criterion, and large-scale velocity field (using FFT to filter out wavenumbers $n > 3$).
Test these functions on the first snapshot. Print key statistics from the first snapshot (e.g., velocity rms, Q-criterion min/max/mean, vorticity magnitude statistics) to the console.
Save a single multi-panel figure containing a 2D slice plot of the Q-criterion and a 2D slice plot of the vorticity magnitude side-by-side to `{database_path}` to verify correctness.
Implement a streaming loader that reads snapshots from `/home/node/work/projects/ns_lagrangian_v1/data/`, keeping only two consecutive snapshots in memory to facilitate linear time-interpolation.

Initialize 5,000 random primary tracers in the domain [-0.5, 0.5]^3. For the first 1,000 of these, initialize 3 auxiliary neighbors displaced by $\epsilon = 10^{-5}$ in the x, y, and z directions (total 8,000 tracers).

Perform RK4 integration with 10 sub-steps per snapshot interval. Use `scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates` for fast trilinear interpolation of the velocity field, with linear time-interpolation between the two loaded snapshots.

Enforce periodic boundary conditions via modulo arithmetic at each sub-step for the 'wrapped' trajectory (used for interpolation). Compute the 'unwrapped' trajectory by accumulating displacements without applying the modulo wrap (tracking true Euclidean displacement from the origin).
At each snapshot time, interpolate the Q-criterion and large-scale velocity (FFT-filtered field, wavenumbers n=1-3 only) at the primary tracer positions.
Save the initial large-scale velocity vector at each tracer's starting position separately (to be used as a fixed reference direction).

Save the unwrapped trajectories (for all 8,000 tracers), wrapped trajectories, and the sampled Q-criterion and large-scale velocity (for the 5,000 primary tracers) as NumPy arrays in `{database_path}`.
Load the primary tracer trajectories, sampled fields, and initial large-scale velocity vectors from `{database_path}`.
Compute the ensemble Mean-Square Displacement (MSD) and the time-dependent power-law exponent $\alpha(t)$ (logarithmic derivative).
Define 'Trapped' (top 20% Q-criterion residence time) and 'Free' (bottom 20%) cohorts, and compute their MSD(t).
Partition tracers into 'Boundary-Crossers' and 'Non-Crossers' based on whether their unwrapped trajectories exceed the domain bounds [-0.5, 0.5], and compute their MSD(t).

Compute $MSD_{\parallel}$ and $MSD_{\perp}$ by projecting tracer displacements onto their initial large-scale velocity vector, and calculate the anisotropy ratio $\lambda(t) = MSD_{\parallel} / MSD_{\perp}$.

Compute the velocity autocorrelation function (VACF) from the tracer velocity time series (obtained by finite-differencing the unwrapped trajectories), and compute the Taylor diffusion coefficient as the time integral of the VACF.

Print all key scalar results to the console: fitted global power-law exponent alpha over the full time range, alpha values for early-time (ballistic) and late-time (diffusive/superdiffusive) regimes separately, mean anisotropy ratio lambda and its standard deviation, and the fraction of tracers classified as Boundary-Crossers.
Save all computed MSDs, $\alpha(t)$, $\lambda(t)$, VACF, and Taylor diffusion arrays to `{database_path}`.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Conditional MSD, Finite-Size Saturation, and Anisotropy Analysis

bullet_points: Load the sampled Q-criterion and the trajectories of the 1,000 tracers and their neighbors from `{database_path}`.

Calculate the autocorrelation function of the Q-criterion along the primary tracer trajectories to determine the decorrelation time of trapping events. Compute and print the Q-criterion decorrelation time (lag at which autocorrelation first crosses zero or drops to 1/e), and compare this value explicitly to the eddy turnover time estimate of ~2.6 time units.
Compute the deformation gradient tensor $F$ for the 1,000 tracers using their neighbors' trajectories, and calculate the Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponent (FTLE) for each tracer over time.
Compute the average FTLE for the 'Trapped' vs 'Free' subsets (among the 1,000 tracers). Print the mean and standard deviation of the FTLE for the Trapped and Free cohorts separately.
Perform and print the result of a simple statistical test (e.g., t-test or Mann-Whitney U test) comparing the two FTLE distributions.
Save the Q-criterion autocorrelation and FTLE results to `{database_path}`.
Load all analysis results from `{database_path}`.
Generate exactly three multi-panel figures to consolidate results.
Figure 1 (MSD-related results): ensemble MSD, conditional MSD (Trapped/Free), $\alpha(t)$, and boundary-crosser MSD.
Figure 2 (Anisotropy and VACF): anisotropy ratio $\lambda(t)$, VACF, and Taylor diffusion coefficient over time.

Figure 3 (Vortex/FTLE diagnostics): Q-criterion autocorrelation, FTLE distribution, Trapped vs Free FTLE comparison (bar chart or time-series), and a 3D spatial visualization of a subset of tracer trajectories overlaid with high Q-criterion regions for the final snapshot.
Save all plots at high resolution (dpi>=300) in `{database_path}`.
Write the full Results section of the paper based on the generated plots and statistics.
Interpret the ballistic-to-superdiffusive crossover, the impact of solenoidal driving on anisotropy ($\lambda$), and the role of coherent structures (Q-criterion) in trapping tracers.

Explicitly address the physical interpretation of the anisotropy ratio lambda in the context of purely solenoidal driving at wavenumbers n=1-3, discussing whether the observed lambda deviates significantly from unity and what this implies about the isotropy assumption commonly made in turbulence models.
Discuss the FTLE results in the context of chaotic vortex interactions and the finite-size effects observed in the boundary-crosser analysis.
Comment on the limitations imposed by the ~4 eddy turnover time window and whether the diffusive limit has been reached.
Ensure all quantitative results and plot references are seamlessly integrated into the academic narrative.
